 This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Come Up For Admission
On 08.11.2019, Along With Wp(C).22187/2015(W), The Court On
The Same Day Delivered The Following:
 WP(C).No.22187 Of 2015(W)&
WP(C).No.17987 Of 2019(W)
 3
 Judgment

These two writ petitions have been heard together on account of the analogous circumstances presented therein and because the reliefs sought for in them are in conflict with each other, thus requiring them to be evaluated together.

2. W.P.(C) No.22187 of 2015 has been filed by a person by name Sri.Aneesh C., impugning Ext.P4 notice issued by Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, asking him to evict himself from the place where he is presently doing the business, alleging that it is unauthorised and therefore, illegal.

Sri.Aneesh says that Ext.P4 is untenable since it has been issued without affording him an opportunity of being heard and also because he is entitled to the benefits of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 ("Street Vendors Act" for short), especially since he has been included in the list of street vendors prepared under it by the competent Town Vending Committee.

entities.text: Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner, therefore, prays that Ext.P4 in this WP(C).No.22187 OF 2015(W)& WP(C).No.17987 OF 2019(W) writ petition be quashed.

3. While so, W.P.(C) No.17987 of 2019 was filed by a person by name Sri.M.M.Yacoob seeking that the afore mentioned order issued by the Corporation to Sri.Aneesh, which has been produced herein as Ext.P6, be implemented and that Sri.Aneesh be removed forthwith from the area where he is doing the business.
The contention of Sri.Yacoob is that he is running a bunk shop under valid permission from the Corporation, while Sri.Aneesh is engaged in a competing business nearby without any such licence.
Sri.Yacoob, therefore, prays that Sri.Aneesh be removed from the area, so that his business will not be in any manner prejudiced.
4. The learned Senior Counsel, Sri.N.Nandakumara Menon, instructed by Sri.P.K.Manojkumar,

learned Standing Counsel for Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, submits that it is not clear from the materials available as to whether either of these petitioners have any right to remain on the footpath or the road margin to do business, as has been asserted by WP(C).No.22187 OF 2015(W)&
WP(C).No.17987 OF 2019(W) them.

He says that Sri.Aneesh has been issued with Ext.P4 notice produced in W.P.(C) No.22187/2015, since admittedly, he has no licence to run the business, but he claims to be a street vendor under the protection of the Street Vendors Act; while Sri.M.M.Yacoob claims to have a licence to erect the bunk and to do business near the Museum area of Thiruvananthapuram though the Corporation is not sure of this.

The learned Senior Counsel says Aneesh C vs The Corporation Of Thiruvananthapuram on 8 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40684839/
3 that, therefore, the Secretary will now hear both parties and decide upon their rival claims, as also their rights to do business in the area concerned, after considering all relevant and germane aspects.

sentences.text:
He says that this is all the more necessary at this time because, as is stated in Annexure A produced along with the statement filed on behalf of the Corporation in W.P.(C) No.17987/2019, the Museum area in Thiruvananthapuram is a very congested one and continuation of illegal businesses and bunks there causes great amount of public prejudice and poses great threat to safety.
5.

When I consider the afore submissions, it is obvious WP(C).No.22187 OF 2015(W)&
WP(C).No.17987 OF 2019(W) that the materials before me do not really establish the rights of either of the petitioners in these writ petitions conclusively though both of them claim either to have a licence from the Corporation or to have the benefit under the Street Vendors Act.

I am, therefore, of the view that this is an imminently fit case where the Secretary of the Corporation must consider their claims, after hearing them, and then take a final decision as to the continuation of these two writ petitioners in the area where they are presently doing their business.

In the afore circumstances, I order both these writ petitions and direct the Secretary of the Corporation to hear the petitioners and evaluate their respective claims - that Sri.M.M.Yacoob is conducting the business based on a valid licence; while Sri.Aneesh C. is entitled to do the business in his capacity as a street vendor protected by the Street Vendors Act.

The Secretary shall, thereafter,
issue an appropriate order with respect to both these petitioners as per law and pursue necessary steps with respect to any action that may be found warranted after the afore exercise,
WP(C).No.22187 OF 2015(W)& WP(C).No.17987 OF 2019(W) without any further delay.
I clarify that the process of hearing the petitioners and issuance of the consequential orders shall be done by the Secretary of the Corporation, as expeditiously as is possible, but not later than two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment; and needless to say, until such time as the afore exercise is completed, both parties will be allowed to continue their businesses, at the places where they are presently doing so, subject to all other requirements in law.
Sd/-
